News.title: Student, 22, ‘shot dead by cops after mistakenly trying to get into stranger’s home after night out with friends’
News.content:
A 22-YEAR-OLD student has been shot dead by police after mistakenly trying to get into a stranger’s home after a night out, his family have claimed.

College baseball catcher Glenn “Bubba” Pysher had thought the home was his mate’s house and knocked on the door before he was shot dead, his mother said.



Mum Erin Pysher said her son had been out celebrating a friend’s birthday at a bar in Upper Pottsgrove, Pennsylvania, when the celebration moved to a pal’s house.

Glenn decided to walk.



Erin told 6ABC: “He ended up at the wrong house after having a few drinks.

“He didn’t know that, so he was knocking on the door saying, ‘Hey, let me in,’ thinking it was his friend’s house, but it wasn’t.”



The couple inside the home on the outskirts of Philadelphia were startled and called the cops.

Police rushed to the scene, responding to a 911 call of a possible attempted break-in at the home Glenn had tried to enter, the Montgomery District Attorney’s Office said.

Cops said they found Glenn at the back of the house and an “encounter ensued” that lead officers to fatally shoot him.

Erin claimed: “12:32, he was on the phone with his friends.



“By 12:35, I believe he’s already shot.

“So, within a few minutes, the cop pulled up and shot him.”

She said her son had been “unarmed”, carrying just “a cell phone and a book bag”.



Erin described her son as a “wonderful young man” who was set to start at Saint Elizabeth University in New Jersey on Monday.

He had recently transferred school and was excited to start on their baseball team, she said.

The heartbroken mum said the college student was a “lovable goofball”.

She said: “He will walk in the back door and say his favorite thing, ‘Hey mom, your favorite kid is home.’

“He was just happy-go-lucky. Didn’t have a care in the world, and I’m going to miss that.”



Family friend Kia told Fox 29: “To see someone that has so much potential because he was so excited about going back to school, lose their life, it hurts.

“He was an amazing soul, young man, never got in any trouble, well-respected.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The fatal shooting was caught on CCTV cameras, police said, adding that the footage would be reviewed as part of the investigation.

The incident is under investigation by the Montgomery County Detective’s Bureau, the local district attorney’s office said.

News.title: Brit soldier dies on holiday in Bali as devastated family face ‘unimaginable pain’ after ‘worst nightmare’
News.content:
HOLIDAY TRAGEDY Brit soldier dies on holiday in Bali as devastated family face ‘unimaginable pain’ after ‘worst nightmare’

A BRITISH soldier has died while on holiday in Bali with his heartbroken loved ones facing “every family’s worst nightmare”.

Finlay John Perkins, known to close friends as Fin, was on a trip to the popular tourist island in Indonesia when he passed away on August 9.



The soldier was in his early twenties with his cause of death yet to be confirmed.

His devastated family said they hoped the holiday would be filled with laughter and treasured memories when they jetted out of the UK earlier this month.



It quickly turned into a nightmare when a young and healthy Finlay tragically died.

Finlay, from the Milton Keynes area, has been remembered as a caring and selfless soldier who always put others first.



A GoFundMe appeal was launched to cover the cost of repatriating the soldier back home.

Over £17,000 has been raised so far from over 550 donors.

The family have now paused the donations as they honoured Finlay by saying: “Forever loved. Forever remembered. Never forgotten.”

The appeal added: “It is with broken hearts that we share the sudden and tragic loss of Cfn Perkins, who passed away whilst on holiday with friends and family.



“No one ever expects a trip filled with laughter, memories, and time spent with loved ones to end in such heartbreak.

“What should have been treasured moments together has instead become every family’s worst nightmare.”

The touching tribute went on to call the brave Brit a son, brother and a loyal friend to all who knew him.



“He was the type of person who would put others before himself, offer a helping hand without hesitation, and bring a smile to those around him,” it continued.

“His loss has left a void that can never truly be filled.”

Finlay’s heartbroken family were the first to announce his death.

They said: “There are no words for how much you’ll be missed, but your grandad and best friend, Aidan, have been reunited with an absolute legend.

“We will forever love you with all our hearts.”



The Royal British Legion, a charity supporting UK veterans and serving soldiers, also paid tribute to Finlay.

It said: “We’re very sorry to hear of the passing of Cfn Perkins, and send our deepest condolences to his family, comrades and loved ones.

“We’d also like to extend our practical support to his family – please do feel free to contact us to discuss what we can do to help.”

When his body is repatriated to the UK, he is expected to be given a public send off.

Family and friends have been invited to escort him on foot from the old police station on Newport Pagnell High Street to St Peter and St Paul’s Church.



The ceremony is planned for September 10.

Mourners will later gather to celebrate what his family have described as his “adventurous life”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The family have asked for any future donations and funeral gifts to be sent to the Jack the Lad charity which campaigns for safer holidays for young British tourists.

The Sun has contacted the FCDO for comment.

News.title: Arguments erupt over ‘queue-jumping tourists’ on popular UK mountain as hikers forced to wait hours to touch summit
News.content:
TEMPERS are peaking on a popular UK mountaintop over hikers who are skipping the hour-long waits to the summit.

Videos of backpackers heckling brazen queue-jumpers racing to Snowdon’s peak have divided viewers on social media.



Some argue you shouldn’t have to queue to reach the summit, while others see it as a shameless violation of British etiquette.

One video shows Mark Screeton, from Manchester, being booed at as he ignored the queue, before he retorts: “Imagine queueing on a mountain? No chance.”



But it’s not all about courtesy, with some pointing out the safety risks of queue-jumping.

“I think you should queue because it’s really quite dangerous and everyone’s trying to get up there – it’s just not safe,” hiker Lucy Taylor told BBC Wales.



Others sympathised with outcast Mark, with Tina Millard from West Bromwich saying: “We’re not at Alton Towers for a ride.

“It’s a mountain, it’s for everyone.”

Visitors at Snowdon likened the atmosphere at the peak to a carnival in recent weeks, due to the huge crowds flocking to the summit.

The bottlenecks are said to have grown in the past month, with the hot weather bringing more hikers to the iconic UK beauty spot.

A spokesperson for Eryri National Park Authority has said policy at the summit remains one of self-regulation.



He said: “There are three quarters of a million people summitting annually, so queues are likely to be expected in peak times.”

He added there were no plans for new measures to be introduced this year, but that the matter would be reviewed in early autumn.

The park has issued reminders to visitors to keep the trails clean and not to disturb wildlife.

Standing at 1,085 metres above sea level, the mountain park, also known as Snowdonia, is a popular destination for hikers, attracting nearly four million a year.

The Princess of Wales was among the thousands of visitors to the summit this summer, who braved the trail on her own in June.



Kate completed the Three Peaks Challenge – which includes Ben Nevis, Scafell Pike and Snowdon – in just 24 hours.

The Princess took on the hike to raise money for The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity and to “explore life beyond diagnosis“.

At the finish line, she was welcomed by the Prince of Wales, their children – Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis – as well as her parents, Carole and Michael Middleton, and her brother, James Middleton.

It follows a similar incident back in May, when two charity hikers were scoffed at for bypassing queues.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Jamie Richardson, 32, and Richard Thiedeman, 34, were met by a jeering crowd after taking different routes to the summit.



Remarking on the reaction, Jamie said: “There’s no policing of it at all, it is purely free will, if you want to queue you can.”

News.title: Glam beauty queen, 24, ‘attacked woman with red stiletto heel in row over taxi outside ball’ – days after Miss GB finals
News.content:
BEAUTY BRAWL Glam beauty queen, 24, ‘attacked woman with red stiletto heel in row over taxi outside ball’ – days after Miss GB finals

A BEAUTY queen who attacked another woman with a red stiletto heel while waiting in a taxi queue after a night out has been spared jail.

Taylor Gidley, 24 – who was crowned Miss Lancashire 2024 – left her victim with a 2cm gash in her cheek after the attack in Preston, Lancashire.



Gidley had attended the Holcombe Harriers Hunt Ball at Owd Nells Tavern before setting upon the woman on October 24, 2024.

Preston Crown Court heard Gidley had screamed at her victim after she approached a man in the taxi queue and asked to share a cab.



She then used her right shoe to strike the woman in the face, sending her flying to the floor in a daze, before continuing to hit her, the court heard.

Her victim, who could not remember the attack when quizzed by cops, told how she “feels anxious when I go out” due to the scar on her face.



Gidley repeatedly sobbed in the dock as recorder Ben Lawrence sentenced her to nine months in jail, suspended for 12 months.

A week before the attack, Gidley had competed in the Miss GB national finals, where she eventually lost out to Miss Edinburgh Ava Morgan.



Prosecutor Mia Monahan told the court there was a shortage of taxis at the pub and the women had asked various people if they could share.

Witnesses told how Gidley then confronted another woman in the queue for cabs before striking her in the face with the stiletto.

One of the victim’s friends said she had complained of pain in her head and had been sick, the court heard.

She woke with a 2cm cut to her cheek and later went to hospital, with her injury found to be consistent with having been struck with a small object.

Gidley was identified through social media and arrested the following day.



She was released under investigation but arrested again on December 15 after officers found the dress and stilettos from the attack at her home.

Gidley told officers she was acting in self defence and did not intend to cause an injury.

She later pleaded guilty to section 20 wounding at Preston Crown Court.

Joe Allman, defending, said there were a number of references which described Gidley as “kind, caring, empathetic and considerate”.

He said the incident was “entirely out of character”.



Her victim told the court: “I now have a scar on my face. I feel it is very noticeable and I am always self conscious.

“I feel anxious when I go out. It is not a normal thing to be hit in the face with a heel and it has taken a long time to process it.

“I don’t like to be around drunk people – it makes me question whether that is what they are all like.”

Sentencing, the judge said: “It seems like you were angered by her asking a male you knew whether they could share a taxi.

“Whatever the cause of your anger it was wholly unjustified, which I am assured you agree with and I have no doubt it was influenced by your consumption of alcohol.



“You had in your hand one of your stiletto heels and you hit her in her cheek with that stiletto.

“She fell to the floor in a daze or unconscious and her friend said you continued to hit her.”

However he accepted the incident was out of character and Gidley had not committed any offences before or since.

Alongside her suspended sentence, Gidley, of Forest Green, Padiham, was ordered to carry out 120 hours of unpaid work.

Throughout the hearing, Gidley sobbed in the dock, dressed in a white shirt and brown trousers.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

She was crowned Miss Lancashire in June 2024 at the Crow Wood Hotel & Spa in Burnley.

The competition raises money for the charity A-sisterhood, which seeks to support, empower and protect women worldwide.

News.title: Full list of GCSE exam resit dates for Maths, English and Science – and how much does it cost?
News.content:
THOUSANDS of pupils returned to school last Thursday to open their long-awaited GCSE results.

After GCSE pass rates were revealed to have slumped to a seven-year low, many students are now weighing up their resit options.

Resit dates have already been scheduled for a number of core school subjects, providing relief to students who may have missed the mark.



Students are able to resit GCSE English Language and Maths in the upcoming autumn term, with all boards scheduling exams between November 3 and 9.



In England, students who do not pass both English Language and Maths are expected to retake the subjects until they receive a necessary grade 4, with around 30 per cent of students facing core subject resits.

The Department for Education says: “Since 2014, the maths and English condition of funding (CoF) requires all students who did not achieve a GCSE grade 4 or above in maths, English or both to continue studying an appropriate qualification.”

If a school, college or training provider fails to make specific students study GCSE English and Maths, they can lose government funding and money.

For any other subject, including English Literature and Sciences, it is not compulsory for a pupil to resit, and they will have to wait until the summer exam period in May and June 2027 to do so.

A number of exam boards have already released the scheduled dates for their English Literature and Science resits, including a list for other optional subjects.

For English Literature, all pupils will complete the first paper on May 12, 2027 and the second paper on May 19, 2027.

Those who achieved a grade 4 or above, and want to get a higher grade, may have to pay a fee, with schools charging as much as between £75 and £150 per exam, with some third- party agencies charging up to £500.

News.title: Britain’s youngest female paedo who abused girls as young as two set to be freed from prison for SECOND time
News.content:
BACK ON THE STREETS Britain’s youngest female paedo who abused girls as young as two set to be freed from prison for SECOND time

BRITAIN’S youngest female paedo who abused children as young as two is set to be freed from prison for a second time.

Sophie Elms was just 17 when she targeted the two pre-school age girls and took photos of the abuse to send to a sex offender she met online.



The childcare student was jailed for seven years and ten months in 2019 after admitting 16 child sex offences.

Elms – now aged 19 – was released from prison in September but recalled after breaking her licence conditions.



But the fiend is now due to walk the streets again this month after being freed for a second time.

A Prison Service spokesperson said: “These were horrendous crimes, and our thoughts remain with the victims.

“Upon release, this offender will be subject to the strict conditions of the sex offender’s register.”

Elms sexually abused two young girls and sent it to another paedophile.

Swindon Crown Court heard she als took indecent photographs of a third girl and downloaded other indecent images from the internet.

The paedo committed most of the sickening offences when she was 17, although the offending began when she was 16.



Police seized four phones that contained indecent images and videos that fell under Category A – the most serious group.

She pleaded guilty to two charges of sexual assault by penetration, two charges of sexual assault by touching, four charges of taking indecent images, six charges of distributing incident images and two charges of possessing extreme pornography.

None of the offences took place at the nursery or college from her childcare course.

During her sentencing in 2019, families of the victims described the impact as “unimaginable” and “horrific”.

Judge Jason Taylor QC jailed Elms for seven years and 10 months, placed her on the sex offenders register indefinitely and made her subject of a sexual harm prevention order until further order.



He said: “In my judgment you knew precisely what you were doing. Your behaviour had elements of planning, it was sustained and it was extensive.

“You knew it was wrong. You had done safeguarding training. You deceived the parents of these children.”

News.title: Golfball-sized hailstones kill at least 100 pigeons in Spain as tourists warned ‘stay indoors’ amid ferocious storm
News.content:
HUGE hailstones the size of golf balls have killed at least 100 pigeons in Spain – as tourists are warned to stay indoors amid a ferocious storm.

A torrential downpour tore through Tarragona on Monday, causing buildings to collapse, travel chaos, and flooding.



Terrifying footage from the east coast city showed one man being swept down a street as it was turned into a river by the deluge.

Another clip showed part of a shopping centre roof coming down during the hailstorm.



The extreme weather also killed around 100 pigeons in Tarragona Port as they were battered by hail.

Shocking videos showed their lifeless bodies lying on the road following the brutal downpour.

One local said: “The birds didn’t have time to protect themselves and they were victims of the violent storm that hit the area with intense rain, strong gusts of wind and lightning.”

More than 1,000 emergency calls were made as the weather wreaked havoc across the coast and left many in Tarragona without electricity.



Firefighters were scrambled to deal with flooded basements and fallen trees – some of which had crushed cars.

Roads were also shut off by some of the destroyed trees.

Three people are understood to have been injured and rushed to hospital due to the storm.



The weather also disrupted a major sporting event.

The third stage of Spain’s annual Vuelta a Espana, one of cycling’s three “Grand Tours” alongside the Tour de France and the Giro d’Italia, was cancelled after athletes were caught out by the hailstorm.

Riders had to stop and take shelter as they headed towards the Font-Romeu ski resort in the French Pyrenees where they were due to finish.



Event organisers confirmed afterwards the cancellation was for the “safety of riders”.

The extraordinary storm also came amid a series of other freak weather events.

At least 11 people were injured in the early hours of Saturday morning during freak weather in and around the town of Roda de Bera a half-hour drive north of the city of Tarragona.

They included an 18-year-old woman left fighting for her life after a seafront wall collapsed on top of her and another two people.

On Monday, the Balearic Islands were hit by a series of mini-tsunamis.



In San Antonio, Ibiza, a concert had to be suspended as the s’Arenal beach was left flooded.

In Majorca the mini-tsunamis, known locally as rissagues, affected the ports of Alcudia, Andratx and Soller as well as Port Adriano near Magaluf.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The extreme weather phenomena known in the Balearics as rissagues are caused by sudden atmospheric pressure changes rather than earthquakes or seismic activities and are not new to the islands.

News.title: Man and woman arrested as baby found dead at house following reports of ‘critically ill’ child
News.content:
DEATH PROBE Man and woman arrested as baby found dead at house following reports of ‘critically ill’ child

A MAN and a woman have been arrested after a baby was found dead at a house.

Emergency services scrambled to a home after reports of a “critically ill infant”.

Cops arrived at 2.45pm on August 16, after paramedics declared the baby dead at the scene in Crewkerne, Somerset.

The death is being treated as unexplained, with police launching an urgent probe.





A man and a woman have been arrested on suspicion of causing or allowing the death of a child.

A spokesman for Avon and Somerset Police said: “We were called to a residential property in Crewkerne by the ambulance service shortly before 2.45pm on Sunday 16 August.

“They informed us there was a young infant who was critically ill.

“Tragically, the baby was pronounced deceased at the scene.

“At this stage we are treating the cause of this sudden death as unexplained following an initial forensic postmortem examination.”

“A decision was made to arrest a man and a woman on suspicion of causing or allowing the death of a child, so both parties had the opportunity to provide us with an account under caution, while in the presence of any legal representative they wished.

“They have both been released under investigation while enquiries continue.

“Our investigation into what happened remains at a very early stage.



“We would politely ask people not to speculate around the circumstances because there is still a great deal of information we need to ascertain and review to further our understanding of what occurred.

“We appreciate news of this child’s death will cause great sadness, particularly in the local community, however we would like to reassure people we do not believe there is any wider risk to public safety.”

News.title: Man dies in crash after police pursuit
News.content:
Officers said after failing to stop, the Audi made off in the direction of the A46 before travelling back towards Stratford on the A439 Warwick Road where the crash occured.

A number of other cars were damaged during the pursuit, police said.

Supt Steve Flavell said: "Our thoughts are with the families of everyone involved in this collision and we're providing specialist support to them at this extremely difficult time.

"We made a mandatory referral to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) because a death had occurred following police contact.

"They have declared an independent investigation and we will co-operate fully with their investigation."

The A439 Warwick Road remains shut from the Marraway roundabout to its junction with Ingon Lane and Sand Barn Lane.

Warwickshire Police said the road was likely to remain closed for some time with drivers being advised to use alternative routes.

Works were carried out on the road two years ago, aimed at reducing the number of crashes in the area.

Warwickshire County Council added a one-way system, lowered the speed limit and implemented a protected turning lane at the Ingon Lane junction.

Street lighting was also boosted to improve visibility for crossing pedestrians at Fisherman's Car Park.

News.title: Yellow weather warnings issued as thunderstorms and flooding forecast
News.content:
Yellow weather warnings have been issued by the Met Office as heavy rain and thunderstorms are forecast to break out over parts of the UK later this week.

The warnings span Wednesday and Thursday and include parts of east Wales, the Midlands, northern England, East Anglia and southern England - including London.

It is likely to be the one of the most widespread outbreaks of heavy rain across southern and central parts of the UK this summer.

While good news for regions plagued by drought, significant accumulations could lead to flash flooding where the ground is too dry and hard to absorb the downpours. Lightning, large hail and gusty winds are also possible.

News.title: Beyond China's humanoid robots, a quieter machine revolution is unfolding
News.content:
"I take a nap and the world changes," says Chen Tianyu.

His world certainly does. The 28-year-old keeps up with the latest technology by spending his spare time in factories that are switching to automation. That way he knows what to prioritise when teaching his class about artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics.

In front of him, around 30 college students are studying code. One of them is typing furiously as his eyes dart from the screen to the robot: "The idea is it will grab that cylindrical piece and move it over there."

A line of industrial robots are waiting to be programmed, and in another part of the classroom, students are trying to develop robotic medical instruments. As he guides them, Chen declares: "If you are not needed by the world of AI and robotics, then you'll definitely be among those eliminated".

For the people in this room, this is a step - or rather a leap - towards a future that China is meticulously building: Xi Jinping's $20bn (Â£14.7bn) plan to put his country at the forefront of innovation and in direct competition with the US.

The evidence is all around them. They are in the Hangzhou Technician Institute, one of several huge, purpose-built vocational schools that want to churn out the next generation of tech-savvy engineers. The campus sits on the outskirts of Hangzhou, a former imperial capital whose futuristic skyline is just the first hint of its role as a global tech hub.

Across the country, there are more than two million robots working in China's factories - which is more than anywhere else - and they are continuing to scale up at extraordinary speed.

News.title: More than 70,000 social and affordable homes to be built across England over 10 years
News.content:
Ministers have announced where more than 70,000 social and affordable homes will be built in England over the next 10 years as part of an initial allocation of almost Â£10bn, in a bid to address the housing crisis.

Funding has been granted to Greater Manchester, the West Midlands, West Yorkshire, South Yorkshire, North East England, and Liverpool. An additional Â£6bn was previously announced for London.

It is the first part of a wider plan to build 300,000 social and affordable homes across the nation, under the government's Â£39bn social housebuilding programme.

Earlier this year, before he became prime minister, Andy Burnham had called for the entire 10-year Â£39bn affordable housing budget for England to be spent on homes for social rent - which means the cost of the unit is about half that of market rents, and there are strict criteria for who can apply for it.

"I would actually devote all of it to social housing," Burnham told The Social Housing Podcast in May.

But of the new homes announced on Monday, 60% would be for social rent.

Housing minister Matthew Pennycook told BBC Breakfast he did not accept Burnham had failed to meet his previous commitment, saying the government had taken a "pragmatic approach" and wants to "get money out the door".

He said the next tranche of funding would be more focused on council houses - which are usually also classed as homes for social rent.

It is understood ministers decided against giving councils more of the funding announced in the first tranche because they did not believe councils would be in a position to build the required number of social homes.

News.title: Russian stadium says it won't host Kanye West gigs
News.content:
The Russian stadium that was scheduled to host two shows by Ye, the rapper also known as Kanye West, has said the events will no longer take place.

In a social media post, external, St Petersburg's Gazprom Arena said no rental agreement had been signed with the concert promoters. "Accordingly, the concert cannot take place on our site."

West would have been the first major Western performer to play Russia since it invaded Ukraine in 2022. The rapper is trying to rehabilitate his image after years of antisemitic remarks, for which he recently apologised.

Gazprom Arena acknowledged it had received complaints about West's planned appearance and stressed that it "was not and is not" responsible for his booking.

The stadium said in its statement that the sold-out concerts, scheduled for 10 and 11 October, had been organised by the Moscow-based Say Agency.

Posting on its Telegram channel, Say Agency said the stadium's announcement had come as a surprise.

"We learned about [it] at the same time as you did, through the media," the agency wrote. "As of now, the Ye concert has not been canceled," it added in a follow-up message.

"We are trying to contact the venue to find out the reason for the post and resolve the issue. We will keep you updated."

The BBC has contacted West's publicist for a comment on the uncertainty over his Russian shows.

In its statement, Say Agency said it announced the concerts earlier this month based "on an official letter that was approved by" Gazprom Arena.

The stadium subsequently sent a rental agreement, Say Agency claimed, and the agency acknowledged the contract had not yet been signed but said the deadline to do so did not expire until later this week.

Last week, Gazprom Arena had posted enthusiastically about the concerts on social media, calling Ye "the most influential musical artist of our time".

Fans reacted to its latest announcement with disappointment.

"This was the shortest concert of my life," responded one, under Say Agency's Telegram post. "It's a shame that the government is putting obstacles in your way," added another.

There is no indication that authorities intervened in the shows, but there has been opposition to West's booking from some Russian politicians.

Vitaly Milonov, a notorious conservative lawmaker, suggested the star should perform traditional Russian songs instead of his planned setlist, reflecting the anti-Western views of many nationalists.

"Maybe after this he'll stop his disgusting antics and become a normal person," Milonov added in a video statement.

News.title: The grieving family who say the coroners' courts aren't working
News.content:
Sarah thought she knew what she was getting into when she attended a coroner's court in May 2024 to discuss the death of her second cousin.

Her day job as a murder detective meant she was used to courts, to judges, to legal argument. What she wasn't prepared for was a coroner's court. "I felt like I was on trial," she recalls of her first hearing, in Woking, Surrey. "I remember just feeling completely railroadedâ¦ It [was] far more hostile than I had ever expected."

Her cousin, Daniel Lindsay, died in 2023, aged 41. He had lived at a home in Surrey that specialises in caring for people with learning disabilities. Daniel also had Down's syndrome and type 1 diabetes.

As his death was unexpected, his case was referred to the coroner for an inquest.

What followed was one of the most stressful experiences of Sarah's life. She discovered new details about how her cousin lived, and his cause of death. The family initially thought Daniel died from a heart attack - but over the course of the inquest, they learnt that was wrong. She had expected the process to be emotional; what she didn't predict was just how complex and frustrating it would be, at times leaving her tearful and furious.

Coroners examine deaths that are not straightforward, like unexpected or violent deaths, or those that take place in state custody. Every year, thousands of British families rely on these courts for crucial answers. For many, an inquest provides the key interaction with the arms of the state at a time of trauma.

News.title: OnlyFans owner was paid over $700m before his death
News.content:
The late owner of streaming platform OnlyFans was paid more than $700m (Â£513m) in dividends before his death from cancer earlier this year.

Fenix International Ltd, the British company that owns OnlyFans, made $714m in profit before tax last year, it said in its annual report. This is an increase of 5% from 2024.

The site hosts a range of subscription-based content from cooking to fitness videos, but it is best known for pornography and is credited with transforming online adult content by encouraging personal connection between sex workers and subscribers.

Its owner Leonid Radvinsky, who died earlier this year aged 43, bought the site from its British founders in 2018.

OnlyFans employs just 47 people. Companies with such high profits rarely have such small staff - for example, British retail giant Marks and Spencer, which employs over 65,000 people, made Â£671m in profit last year.

Fenix International's company results show that it paid dividends of $535m for the year ending 30 November 2025, with further dividends payments totalling $174m between then and 26 March 2026.

Radvinsky, who was born in Ukraine and raised in the US, died on 23 March. The company is now owned by his widow, Yekaterina 'Katie' Chudnovsky.

OnlyFans surged in popularity during the Covid-19 pandemic, landing Radvinsky on Forbes' annual list of billionaires just three years later.

The site is known for the way it encourages creators and fans to connect through livestreams, personalised messages, and direct requests for custom-made photos and videos.

In return for hosting the material, OnlyFans takes a 20% share of all payments.

The site had 132 million paying subscribers and 2.5 million active creators in 2025.

The boom in size and popularity under Radvinsky's ownership also brought scrutiny from lawmakers and regulators over its adult content â a recent BBC Three documentary uncovered allegations of exploitation, coercion and violence committed against OnlyFans creators.

In 2024, British regulators launched an investigation into whether children were accessing porn, an issue that the company at the time blamed on a technical issue.

Ofcom ultimately dropped that probe, but it fined the firm about Â£1m, external for failing to respond accurately to its requests for information about the measures it had in place to check the age of its users, who in theory must be 18 or over.

Creators have also debunked the narrative that making explicit videos on the site is a get-rich-quick scheme.

Keily Blair, the chief executive of OnlyFans, said on Tuesday that the company had paid over $30bn to creators since launching a decade ago.

"OnlyFans provides real opportunities to real people by creating a safe, regulated space where people can monetise their content with a global fan base," she said.

"As a UK-based business we have also made a significant contribution to the UK economy, paying over Â£600 million in corporate taxes from 2016 to date."

News.title: Burnham refuses to rule out tax rises in autumn Budget
News.content:
Andy Burnham has refused to rule out tax rises in the upcoming autumn Budget, saying he "won't be unrealistic" about the "challenging" state of public finances.

The prime minister said he would take a "careful approach" to the economy, and defended his previously announced cost of living pledges as funded spending commitments.

Burnham became prime minister in July promising to give people breathing space and help with the cost of living, but questions remain over how major policies such as social care reforms will be funded.

Experts have previously warned that he and Chancellor John Healey will have little financial room to manoeuvre in their first Budget on 28 October.

Speaking during his first visit to Ukraine, Burnham said the policies announced so far including capping bus fares at Â£2 and cutting VAT on household electricity bills were "the first steps that I've felt able to make", and were doable because he was able to reprioritise funding from elsewhere.

"I took the decision early on that digital ID wasn't the top priority for now. And so we've reprioritised funding to other priorities," he said in an interview with ITV.

Asked if the public needed to accept some of the new policies would have to be paid for in tax rises, Burnham said they wouldn't necessarily have to accept that.

Pushed on whether he would need to raise taxes to cover spending gaps, he said: "I will always take a careful approach to things. I ran Greater Manchester for 10 years and we ran a very tight ship with rock solid finances.

"Nothing will change as I come into this role as prime minister. I won't take risks with people's jobs or their livelihoods or their family finances.

"I will try to help them in whatever way I can, I have already done some things that will help them."

Burnham previously told the BBC he accepts his earlier announcements aimed at tackling the cost of living are not enough on their own and hinted at further support.

Speaking during his first official overseas visit on Monday, he said while he would do what he could, "I won't be unrealistic and people really need to understand that.

"We are in a challenging position, whatever I do will be carefully thought through, it will be funded and there will be more to come as we go into the autumn."

Last week official figures showed the the government borrowed more than expected in July, despite a record month for income tax receipts.

Inflation also reached a four-month high of 2.9% in July and is expected to rise further due to the ongoing impact of the Iran war, which has hit energy prices and fuel costs.

Experts have warned Burnham and Healey that they need to either raise taxes or cut spending elsewhere as pressure on the public finances has left no room for extra borrowing.

Both the prime minister and chancellor have vowed to stick to the fiscal rules set by former chancellor Rachel Reeves.

The rules are designed to ensure day-to-day spending is funded through tax revenue by the end of the Parliament, and to reduce debt as a proportion of GDP.

Rain Newton-Smith, chief executive of the Confederation of British Industry, said business owners wanted to create opportunities for young people but "the cost of employing people has gone up so much".

"The business leaders I speak to say that the cost of doing business has gone up so much that it's holding them back from creating opportunities," she told the Today programme.

She said targeted support for businesses would create "more growth and more opportunities that saves money for the government and ultimately leads to higher tax receipts".

News.title: Legendary rugby league winger Boston dies aged 92
News.content:
Rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston has died aged 92.

Last year, he became the first player in rugby league's 130-year history to receive a knighthood.

Born in Cardiff in 1934, Boston grew up playing union but - overlooked by his home club - came to the attention of rugby league scouts while on national service in the north of England, signing for Wigan in 1953 as a 19-year-old.

Despite having played just a handful of games in league, the young winger's talent was quickly evident and Boston was picked for the 1954 Great Britain side that went to Australia and New Zealand - becoming the first black British player to tour down under.

He reached the 100-try milestone in just 68 matches after his switch from union.

Boston's scoring ratio is extraordinary, claiming 478 tries in 488 games for Wigan and helping them win three Challenge Cups and the Championship.

News.title: Birth of ospreys chicks on Anglesey is a first, experts say
News.content:
Two osprey chicks have been born on Anglesey for the first time, according to conservationists.

The baby birds were hatched earlier this summer, and have since successfully left the nest, with hopes they may return.

Friends of the Ospreys, the conservation group who monitor the private site, said they were "over the moon" at the news, and hoped it pointed to a bright future for the species on the island.

The adult ospreys responsible for these chicks are one of about 300 breeding pairs in the UK, with about 20 in Wales.

News.title: New 10p coin enters circulation - will you spot one?
News.content:
Something new might appear in your change when you pay in cash from now on: a 10p coin featuring the portrait of King Charles and the world's largest grouse.

Sufficient demand for the coins mean newly-minted 10p pieces are entering circulation for the first time for about four years, this time with a new design.

The Royal Mint says shoppers and collectors should discover the coins, which were minted and dated in 2023 and 2026, across the country.

The reverse side of the coin depicts an image of the capercaillie which is found in a small part of Scotland and threatened with extinction.

The redesigned suite of coins to celebrate the King's love of the natural world were unveiled in October 2023 by The Royal Mint.

The tails side of every newly-minted coin from the 1p to the Â£2 now features the country's flora and fauna - from bees to an oak tree leaf.

Coins in circulation in the UK carrying the portrait of King Charles have so far been limited to the 5p, 50p and Â£1.

Old coins with the image of the late Queen Elizabeth II can still be used, so the new coins are only struck in response to demand.

That is why, with 1.4 billion 10p coins in circulation, there has been no need for the new 10p to be released until now by The Royal Mint.

Now. 600,000 of these coins, dated 2023, and 6.5 million dated 2026 have been released to banks and post offices nationwide.

However, King Charles III coins still only represent about 1% of the 24.1 billion coins in circulation across the UK, making any new ones highly sought after by seasoned numismatists and new coin collectors.

News.title: Organised crime arrests in A66 crash investigation
News.content:
Twelve people have been arrested as part of the investigation into the A66 crash that killed seven people, including two police officers.

Nine men and three women, aged between 19 and 61, have been arrested across Teesside on suspicion of a range of offences including possession of a firearm and being part of an organised crime group. One has since been charged.

In the early hours of Saturday, a Volkswagen Passat that had been pursued by police travelled the wrong way down the A66 near Middlesbrough and crashed into an oncoming police car - two PCs and all five Passat occupants died.

Cleveland Police said it was investigating "serious criminal activity that resulted in this fatal incident".

PC Tom Clough, 38, and PC Matthew Blades, 37, died in the crash, as did Michael Robert Cahill, 23, Jacob Matusiak, 23, Makai Saddington, 18, Theo Rae, 17, and 17-year-old Cole Robert Worthy.

Earlier, Cleveland Police released more details of its investigation into the lead-up to the crash and information about the 12 people it had arrested.

The force said:

It received several reports of two vehicles "being driven dangerously" on Saturday morning

The first vehicle, believed to be a Volvo XC60, was seen "ramming properties" in the Middlesbrough area

The second vehicle, a Passat, is believed to have been associated with this activity

Both vehicles were operating with cloned number plates but were picked up by automated number plate recognition technology

The Volvo has been recovered in Middlesbrough

Four of the five people in the Passat had previous convictions

Assistant Chief Constable Wayne Fox said the investigation had been "fast moving and complex".

He said: "The events of that tragic night will have a lasting and profound impact on the Cleveland area and the communities we seek to protect.

"We have a duty to respond to, and thoroughly investigate, the serious criminal activity that resulted in this fatal incident and to bring all those responsible to justice."

News.title: Letting agent accused of not returning deposits to more than 100 tenants
News.content:
Raman Kaur and her family rented a house through Morgan, Payne & Knightly (MPK) until September 2025 when they bought their own home.

They are still waiting for their Â£900 deposit to be returned and have discovered the money was not put in a registered deposit scheme.

"It's not right, he shouldn't be doing that with our money," she said. "That's our sweat, our hard work.

"It's very stressful having a young family and with the financial crisis that we're all going through.

"We've saved that money, we've budgeted and we've had to tell the kids they can't have things.

"I think he should be ashamed of what he's done. It's not his money, he didn't earn it."

Kaur says the family visited the West Bromwich branch of MPK to resolve the matter, but found it had closed, leaving them to try phoning Singh and his staff every day.

The home the family rented is owned by an individual who did not want to be named in this article. We will refer to him as Vikram.

"I'm owed Â£700 and MPK are falsely saying they're registered in a deposit protection scheme, but they're not," he said.

"I've spent months trying to get hold of Tony Singh but the offices have shut down, and nobody answers the phone or emails.

"It feels like nobody can help us, so we contacted the BBC."

Our investigation has since found that individual sums that are owed range from Â£700 to Â£16,000.

Vikram reported his experience to Trading Standards.

Sandwell Council, which covers West Bromwich, said both Singh and MPK were no longer operating in the borough.

Singh and MPK continue, however, to operate elsewhere in the West Midlands, the BBC can confirm.

News.title: Briton fighting for Russia killed in Ukraine
News.content:
A British national has been killed in Ukraine while fighting for Russia.

Bradley Townsend is said to have died following an attack by a remote-controlled FPV drone in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region. His death, on 10 June, is believed to be the first of a British citizen fighting for Russia in the conflict.

The 33-year-old left his home in Barnsley, South Yorkshire, earlier this year after telling his family he was going to Romania, according to the Yorkshire Post, external.

The Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) confirmed it was aware of reports a British national had died in Ukraine, adding it was in contact with his family.

The news emerged as Andy Burnham arrived in Kyiv for his first foreign trip as UK prime minister.

The visit coincides with the 35th anniversary of the country's independence from the Soviet Union.

The government has agreed to hand over blueprints for British-made components for the Scalp missile, a French version of the UK's Storm Shadow cruise missile - allowing Ukraine to produce the weapon domestically.

News.title: Boy, 16, arrested after four viable devices found in security alert
News.content:
A 16-year-old boy has been arrested under the Terrorism Act after a security alert in Omagh, County Tyrone.

Police carried out a planned search on Monday at an address in the Gardenville Avenue.

Police said four viable explosive devices were found and removed from the property for forensic examination.

Nearby residents who had been asked to leave their homes during the alert have since returned.

Det Insp Winters urged the public not to speculate about the incident.

"It's important to stress that, while the suspect has been arrested under the Terrorism Act, our investigation to establish a motive remains very much ongoing."

News.title: Man charged with murder after house fire
News.content:
A man has been charged with murder, attempted murder and arson following a fire in west London that left a woman dead and eight others in need of hospital treatment.

Pawel Kulpa, 34, faces one count of murder, eight counts of attempted murder and one count of arson with intent to endanger life.

The charges come after a fire at a residential address on Berkeley Avenue, Hounslow, at about 01:15 BST on Wednesday, 19 August.

A 50-year-old woman, named by the Met Police as Anna Kowalska, died in hospital while another woman, 40, remains in hospital in a life-threatening condition. Kulpa is due to appear at Willesden Magistrates' Court on Tuesday.

News.title: Economist faces backlash for saying gig work improves welfare: ‘Flexibility is a benefit’
News.content:

A Chinese professor has sparked a fierce backlash online for describing gig work as a form of welfare, exposing public frustration over job insecurity and the lack of social protection for millions of people.

Zhang Dandan, a prominent economics professor at Peking University, argued during a TV discussion on the employment situation of gig workers that “flexible employment is a welfare benefit”.

“From a labour economics perspective, flexibility itself is a benefit. Unlike us who have fixed 9-5 jobs, although our jobs offer social security and housing fund benefits, those are obtained in exchange for time and freedom,” she said.

Her comments quickly went viral on Chinese social media and were called out for being out of touch and privileged.

The professor did note that while “some people actively choose flexible employment, others have no choice because they cannot find a stable job with a labour contract and social insurance and housing fund benefits”.

She also acknowledged that “income disparity among gig workers is huge”.

open image in gallery A food delivery rider passes by a Foxconn manufacturing complex in Shenzhen, China ( Getty )

China’s gig economy has expanded rapidly as meagre unemployment insurance, record numbers of graduates and job shortages have squeezed opportunities for tens of millions of people.

An estimated 320 million people are currently in flexible employment without a permanent contract, rising from 280 million in 2025, according to the think tank China New Employment Forms Research Centre. That figure accounts for about 44 per cent of China’s total workforce and is as large as the US population.

Gig workers routinely complain of difficult working conditions, long hours, and low or unstable pay.

open image in gallery A food delivery driver walks past the headquarters of the Chinese travel agency Trip in Shanghai ( AFP/Getty )

Prominent commentator Hu Xijin, a former editor of the newspaper Global Times, called Ms Zhang’s framing of gig work “completely unacceptable” and “shocking”.

He noted that most flexible workers took such jobs out of necessity rather than preference. “She has paid the price for her reputation for speaking this way and the responsibility lies with her,” Mr Hu said, adding that the professor should “respond to public opinion, explain where necessary, and apologise where appropriate”.

Ms Zhang’s words also drew criticism from social media users. “Such comments from experts are no less than rubbing salt into the wounds of those without job security,” a Weibo user said.

“Every day, they are racing against their platform’s algorithm at all costs, without rest,” another said, adding that gig work was “precisely the most unavoidable of choices, not a preference”.

open image in gallery A food delivery person for Meituan waits for orders outside a KFC outlet in Beijing ( AFP/Getty )

Ms Zhang’s work focuses on documenting the realities of precarious and flexible work and advocating for better institutional adaptations.

In 2025, she found that on-demand workers made up nearly 31 per cent of the workforce in China’s manufacturing sector. And during peak season, that proportion rose as high as 80 per cent for large manufacturers with more than 10,000 workers.

Her study covered nearly 30 manufacturing firms, 20 labour intermediaries, and 10 labour markets in key manufacturing hubs across the country.

News.title: Rugby League legend Billy Boston dies aged 92
News.content:

We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

One of Rugby League’s most legendary stars, Sir Billy Boston, has died at the age of 92.

Boston was an rugby icon, a trailblazer for black players and the very first rugby league player to be awarded a knighthood - which he received in 2025 - ending the sport’s 130-year wait for the honour.

He was born in Cardiff in 1934 and grew up playing rugby union before making the switch to rugby league and signing for Wigan Warriors in 1953 at 19-years-old.

A year later after just a few matches for Wigan, Boston was selected for Great Britain and faced Australia and New Zealand becoming the first non-white player to tour down under.

open image in gallery Sir Billy Boston was hailed as “simply the greatest” by Wigan head coach Matt Peet (PA Archive) ( PA Archive )

He excelled for Wigan across 488 appearances and ended his career with a British-record 571 tries, 478 of which were scored for the Warriors. During his time with Wigan he helped the club to win three Challenge Cups and the Championship.

He reached the 100-try milestone in just 68 matches after his switch from union and featured in six Challenge Cup finals with his three wins coming in 1958, 1959 and 1965.

Boston also scored 24 tries in 31 appearances for Great Britain and was part of the 1960 World Cup winning team having scored a try in the final against Australia.

After his retirement from rugby, Boston ran the Griffin Hotel in Wigan and had a stand at Wigan's Central Park Ground named after him. Sadly, the ground was demolished in 1999 and the hotel has since fallen into disrepair.

open image in gallery Sir Bill Boston was the first rugby league player to be awarded a knighthood which he received off King Charles III in 2025 ( Getty )

In1988, Boston was also one of the first players inducted into the Rugby League Hall of Fame and is featured as one of five rugby league stars included in a statue at Wembley Stadium. There is another statue of him in his home city of Cardiff and a third in Believe Square in Wigan.

Boston was also appointed an MBE in 1986 and was inducted into the Welsh Sports Hall of Fame, when it was launched in 1990.

Following a diagnosis of vascular dementia in 2016, at the age of 82, Boston’s death comes just weeks after the passing of his wife, Lady Joan.

Tributes have come flooding in for the rugby league legend with Wigan Warriors owner Mike Danson saying: "Billy Boston was everybody's hero, including my Mum's.

"His achievements in rugby league were extraordinary, and his knighthood was a fitting recognition of a career that brought great credit to Wigan and to the game.

"But Billy's legacy was not simply what he achieved. It was the humility with which he carried it. Despite everything he accomplished, he remained a quiet, dignified and deeply respected man. He leaves behind an example that will endure for generations. Our thoughts are with his family and those closest to him.

"A great man, and a true Wigan legend. He will be remembered with pride and affection."

open image in gallery Tributes have come in from the across rugby league paying respect to Boston’s legacy ( PA Archive )

Warriors head coach Matt Peet added: “On behalf of myself, our coaching staff and players, from the first team through to our academy, we send our deepest condolences to Sir Billy’s family, friends and loved ones at this incredibly sad time.

“Billy Boston is woven into the fabric of this club... those fortunate enough to have seen him play tell me he was simply the greatest. His achievements, the man he was and the standards he set will continue to inspire everyone who pulls on this shirt.

“His legacy goes far beyond records and trophies. His impact on Wigan, on rugby league and on the wider sporting world was recognised at the very highest level. We will do everything we can to honour his memory by representing this club with the pride, humility and excellence that he embodied.

“Sir Billy Boston will always be one of Wigan Warriors’ greatest sons, and he will never be forgotten.”

In a released statement, Wales Rugby League said: "Today, rugby league has lost one of its greatest ever players, Wales has lost one of its finest sporting sons, and our sport has lost a truly special gentleman."

Hulu has decided not to renew Mindy Kaling’s Gen Z comedy series Not Suitable For Work for a second season.

The sitcom, created by Kaling, starred Ella Hunt (AJ), Avantika Vandanapu (Abby), Will Angus (Davis), Jack Martin (Josh), Nicholas Duvernay (Kel) and Jay Ellis (Bill) “five work-obsessed 20-somethings striving for professional success” in Manhattan’s Murray Hill neighborhood.

Season one aired in June and ran for nine episodes.

Variety reports that Warner Bros. TV, which produces the series, plans to shop it to other companies.

Kaling’s representatives did not immediately respond to The Independent’s request for comment.

open image in gallery Mindy Kaling’s latest sitcom has been abandoned by Hulu after one season ( Getty )

open image in gallery Will Angus and Jack Martin star in 'Not Suitable for Work,' which follows a group of Gen Z friends in Murray Hill ( Disney )

The season ended with a number of loose ends for its characters,

NSFW drew mixed reviews upon its release, earning an overall critics’ score of 54 percent on Rotten Tomatoes. However, audiences responded better, giving it an overall score of 82 percent on the review aggregation site.

In her review for Variety, Alison Herman branded it a “bland Friends copycat with hints of a sharper show.”

The cast have not shied away from comparisons to the classic sitcom, however, with Duvernay previously telling The Hollywood Reporter: “It’s always had a bit of a Friends vibe. That’s a giant to compare it to, but that’s initially how I felt being part of it. It has a more modern take on it. It’s work-obsessed kids trying to make their way in New York.”

Kaling broke out in Hollywood as Kelly Kapoor in NBC’s The Office, which she helped write, produce and direct during its eight-season run.

She went on to create, write, produce, and star in The Mindy Project, which premiered on Fox in 2012. The sitcom, about an ambitious New York OB/GYN navigating her career and romantic life, ran for three seasons on Fox before being rescued by Hulu, where it continued for another three seasons, ending in 2017

She has since established herself as a prolific producer and creator, developing shows including Champions, Four Weddings and a Funeral, Never Have I Ever, The Sex Lives of College Girls, Velma and Netflix’s Running Point, which has already been renewed for a third season.

Not Suitable for Work completed Kaling’s loosely autobiographical trilogy, which began with Never Have I Ever, following an Indian-American high school student in California, continued with The Sex Lives of College Girls, and concluded with NSFW, which follows post-college life in New York.

Widespread floods triggered by heavy rain from Typhoon Narra intensified on Tuesday across southern China, with homes and shops submerged and thousands of people relocated, while another storm system made its way towards Japan and Taiwan.

Authorities in Chongzuo, in China's Guangxi region famous for its giant waterfalls and karst limestone mountains, evacuated more than 15,000 people after water levels surpassed a record high set in 2008.

Meanwhile, medium-strength Typhoon Saudel moved towards southern Japan and northern Taiwan where it is expected to bring sporadic heavy rain, as Taiwan reported one dead and four missing from a separate weather system over ⁠its south and east.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

Rising floodwaters have prompted China to relocate a total of 54,000 people in Guangxi, state television said.

Narra has lingered ⁠over the Beibu Gulf, also known as the Gulf ​of ⁠Tonkin, in the northwestern part of the South China Sea for several days, dumping heavy rain on Guangxi and the nearby provinces of Hainan and Guangdong.

Heavy rain is expected to persist across parts of Vietnam and southern China through Wednesday, with areas of Guangxi, Guangdong, Hainan and Fujian forecast to receive torrential rain, state media said.

In Chongzuo, river water overflowed into the city, with water levels reaching the rooftops of some buildings and power lines.

A notice from Chongzuo authorities on Monday ordered all businesses and tourist operations to cease and urged evacuated residents not to return to high-risk areas.Japan's weather agency warned of destructive gusts as Typhoon Saudel approached the southwestern islands of Okinawa prefecture, also causing extremely strong winds and high seas.

open image in gallery ( Reuters )

Saudel is expected to pass to the north of Taiwan and dump water on its north starting late Thursday and into Friday, though its intensity is forecast to gradually weaken and its storm-force wind radius to shrink, the island's Central Weather Administration said.

However, there is uncertainty about the timing and extent of the typhoon's rainfall ‌impact, it added.

In southern and eastern Taiwan, the government reported one person dead and four missing from a tropical depression that brought flooding in the cities of Tainan and Kaohsiung, home to more than four million people.

During the three days from Sunday to Tuesday, almost a metre (3.9ft) ⁠of rain fell in Kaohsiung, which the government said exceeded rainfall during 2009's devastating Typhoon Morakot that killed about 700 people ‌and caused damage of up ​to $3bn.

Saudel is forecast to hit the coast in the southeastern Chinese province of Fujian from late Thursday to early Friday.

Garmin has launched the Fenix 9, a new and updated version of its flagship smartwatch.

The Fenix line is marketed as being for “serious athletes and adventurers”, though it also represents the most expensive and high-end product in Garmin's main line-up. As such, it tends to be the product through which the company shows off its newest and most advanced features.

This time around, the update brings a dramatically improved screen – which Garmin says is twice as bright as the previous Fenix 8 – as well as new training tools and better maps. But it also brings a first look at Garmin’s new “Epic” feature, aimed at making it easier to share long adventures.

The new training tools appear relatively iterative when compared with the previous Fenix 8, which was released in August 2024. Garmin pointed to better tracking of stamina and endurance to understand how much energy a user might have to give to an exercise, and improved tracking of rowing activities that can now give a better picture of someone’s fitness.

Garmin also pointed to the better maps that are included in the device. It said that routing will now be “smoother and more intuitive” thanks to the changes.

The “Epic” feature appeared to be primarily focused on collating and sharing activities after they are done, and on the phone, though it includes changes on the device, too. Garmin pointed to the example of someone undertaking a long hike, and stitching together the activities so that friends and followers can see one big map and details of a trip.

As Garmin’s flagship watch, the Fenix 9 also benefits from all the exercise features that the company has brought to its recent watches. That includes detailed activity tracking, precise location data during activities, and fitness and wellness features that aim to provide feedback both before and after activities.

It also benefits from Garmin’s wellness tools, such as energy burn through the day, as well as smartwatch features including notifications from the phone, a microphone and speaker to talk to virtual assistants such as Siri, and integration with other apps such as WhatsApp and Spotify.

The Fenix 9 will be available to order on 28 August. It starts at £849 in the UK, all the way up to £1,200 for the largest, pro version with Garmin’s satellite messaging features and solar charging.

The watch had been scheduled to launch in a live event at noon UK time. But on Tuesday morning, details of the Fenix 9 were posted to Garmin's official website.

Police have condemned “unacceptable” driving behaviour after several vehicles were caught driving in the wrong direction on the motorway following a crash.

Multiple drivers were seen trying to avoid traffic delays by going the wrong way back up the M6 slip road near junction 34 in Lancaster on Sunday.

It comes after seven people, including two officers, were killed in a crash on Saturday after a vehicle drove the wrong way down the A66 in South Bank struck a police car.

In a statement, Lancashire Police said: “Thankfully nobody was seriously hurt, either in the collision or due to this incident, but as we have seen in other parts of the country this weekend, these actions can have utterly devastating consequences.

“We have identified a number of those vehicles and drivers involved in the incident and will take the appropriate action against them.

“We know that there will have been a lot of people on the motorway or making their way the correct direction down the slip road at that time, who will have been lawfully going about their journeys.”

open image in gallery Two police officers and five young men were killed in South Bank, near Middlesbrough, on Saturday ( PA )

Following the fatal collision in Middlesbrough on Saturday, Matt Storey, the Cleveland police and crime commissioner, hit out at an “absolutely idiotic” social media trend showing people driving the wrong way down roads.

Research shows that a driver appears in court every week for risking a head-on collision by driving the wrong way on the motorway.

The government has told TikTok and other social media platforms to remove content featuring the trend, describing the glorification of dangerous driving as “utterly disgraceful”.

Mr Storey told Radio 4’s Today programme: “Without being able to say whether that was anything like involved in this case, it’s absolutely idiotic for anybody to be doing anything other than being completely 100 per cent focused on the road when they’re behind the wheel of a vehicle.”

Jakub Matusiak, one of the young men who died, had previously shared footage on his social media showing him driving recklessly and barreling through a neighbourhood. It is not yet clear whether the men killed were following the trend.

open image in gallery Lancashire Police have urged for people to people to come forward with footage ( PA Archive )

Speaking of the latest wrong-way driving incident, Lancashire Police added: “Being stuck in standstill or slow-moving traffic can be frustrating, we get it, but it is never an excuse to put the lives of those around you, and your own life at risk.

“Nobody got hurt yesterday, but that outcome could have so easily been different. We will not tolerate driving that endangers lives.”

The force is urging anyone with dashcam or mobile phone footage that could show any drivers involved in the incident to come forward.

“If you have information or footage that can help us, please call 101 quoting log 0689 of 23rd August,” it said in a statement.

The European Court of Human Rights on Tuesday criticized Turkey's courts over the imprisonment of prominent philanthropist Osman Kavala, saying it highlighted a “systemic problem” that was “marked by the detention and prosecution of political opponents, human-rights defenders and journalists.”

Kavala, 68, the founder of a nonprofit organization promoting peace and dialogue, was sentenced to life in prison without parole in 2022 on charges linked to 2013 protests and a coup attempt in 2016.

Human rights advocates and opposition groups say President Recep Tayyip Erdogan ’s government has weaponized the judiciary to target critics and rivals after more than two decades in power.

Reiterating a call for Kavala’s release it first made in 2019, the European court said his conviction should be regarded as “as null and void.” In a statement, the court said Turkey had violated several of Kavala’s fundamental rights.

The violations “also revealed structural shortcomings which affected the guarantees of independence and impartiality of the judiciary, and which were likely to facilitate the exerting of direct or indirect influence by the executive branch on certain judicial decisions, particularly in cases with a sensitive political dimension,” the France-based court added.

The Turkish government maintains that the justice system is impartial and independent. Erdogan has dismissed the court’s previous rulings, saying Turkey would not “recognize those who do not recognize our courts.”

Kavala was first detained in 2017 on accusations that he financed protests four years earlier that attempted to overthrow the government. He was acquitted in 2020, but was swiftly rearrested on charges linking him to Turkey’s 2016 coup attempt.

His acquittal was overturned and the case was merged with that relating to the coup attempt. He was sentenced to life in prison without parole in April 2022.

The case led to a diplomatic crisis in 2021 when Erdogan threatened to declare 10 foreign ambassadors, including the U.S., French and German representatives in Ankara, persona non grata after they called for Kavala's release.

News.title: Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea
News.content:
“I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”

Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”

If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.

There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

News.title: Help us test binoculars with the RSPB and birding experts
News.content:
At Telegraph Recommended, we test hundreds of products each year, and we rely on our community members to help verify our experts’ findings.

We currently have an upcoming opportunity for Telegraph readers to help test the latest binoculars for birdwatching with the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB).

Selected readers will be invited to RSPB’s The Lodge nature reserve in Sandy, Bedfordshire, where Jamie Wyver, editor of the RSPB magazine, and Tim Jones, otherwise known as ‘Begin Birding’ on Instagram, will host two binocular testing mornings.

Taking place on September 23 and 24, Jamie and Tim will lead each group on a morning ramble across the heathland, offering the chance to spot local bird species, including Nightjars, Hobbies and Spotted Flycatchers.

News.title: This summer’s wildfire epidemic is one of the worst in decades – so why are deaths so low?
News.content:
Wildfires in Britain and Europe this year are among the worst in decades, yet direct deaths are at some of the lowest levels, according to a Telegraph analysis.

As of early August, 505,683 hectares of land have burned across Europe, forcing the evacuation of more than 360,000 people as uncontrollable flames reach major cities, towns, and villages.

The problem is global – in the US, Nevada declared a state of emergency over the weekend after a wildfire caused more than 42,000 people to evacuate their homes.

But what sets 2026 apart isn’t just the vast areas of land burned, but how few deaths have been caused by the fires.

This summer, just 14 people are reported to have died in European wildfires, the vast majority in a single blaze in Almería, southern Spain.

By comparison, more than 130 people were killed in the summer of 2017 – a toll driven largely by the Pedrógão Grande disaster in Portugal, where more than 60 people died on a single stretch of road.

In 2018, at least 100 others died in a single afternoon in the Mati disaster near Athens, despite total hectares burned that year being roughly a third of current levels.

Since the modern phenomenon of summer wildfires exploded in Europe a decade ago, the direct death toll has broadly trended downward, as the chart below shows.

News.title: Swine flu outbreak in Delhi swamps clinics and hospitals
News.content:
India is battling a surge in H1N1 flu infections, prompting the federal health ministry to step up surveillance and hospital preparedness.

The national capital New Delhi has recorded 1,777 cases this year, almost eight times the number (229) reported during the same period in 2025.

Dr Randeep Guleria, a senior pulmonologist and director of Medanta Medical School, Gurugram, says the H1N1 cases are much higher than reported.

“It’s quite likely that the reported numbers are an underestimate because they depend on how many people are tested,” Guleria said. “If you speak to patients admitted to hospital who test positive for H1N1, you often find that other members of their family have similar symptoms, although they have not been tested.”

“There is a surge and we are seeing a lot of patients. We are testing only those who come to hospital and are more seriously ill,” Guleria said.

H1N1, commonly known as swine flu, is a subtype of influenza A. It is a contagious respiratory infection that can cause fever and cough and in severe cases it can lead to pneumonia and respiratory failure.

Officials at the Indian Council of Medical Research said the rise did not mean the emergence of a new strain of the virus.

The surge comes during India’s rainy season, when seasonal influenza and other respiratory infections typically increase.

Doctors in Delhi say they are seeing more patients with high fevers, persistent coughs and flu-like symptoms, although most cases remain mild.

The H1N1 cases have been reported beyond New Delhi. The metro cities like Mumbai, Chennai and Bangaluru have reported a high number of cases, although the pattern is not uniform across the country.

Doctors in Bangaluru have reported more influenza A infections among children, with some developing pneumonia and respiratory distress.

India’s health minister JP Nadda said there was a need for continued vigilance and robust surveillance. He has asked officials to monitor unusual increases and clusters of cases and ensure hospitals could respond quickly.

“Swine flu (H1N1) can show up through symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue… If you experience these symptoms, seek medical advice at your nearest healthcare centre,” the health ministry said on X.

Delhi’s health minister, Pankaj Kumar Singh, said the capital had enough beds, doctors, medicines and medical equipment to manage the increase. “Delhi is fully prepared to deal with the present health situation,” Singh said.

India has had several waves of H1N1 since the virus emerged globally in 2009.

The infection, commonly called swine flu, became a recurring seasonal respiratory illness after the 2009 pandemic rather than disappearing from circulation.

India recorded 3,320 H1N1 cases and 14 deaths in 2025, according to Ministry of Health data.
